description: Workspace/CI restructure for the networked providers crate, plus the provider contract, registry, and shared HTTP/SSE + capability foundation (tasks P2.1, P2.2, P2.3). Because the providers crate gains crates.io deps (HTTP client + SSE + async trait), move it from `members` to `exclude` in hybrid-orchestrator/Cargo.toml and add explicit per-manifest CI steps, mirroring the documented pattern used for domain/orchestrator-core/persistence/secrets/tauri-app. This feature establishes everything the adapters build on. This crate CANNOT compile in the offline sandbox (crates.io 403); its build/test/clippy are DEFERRED TO CI. Verify offline that the rest of the workspace still builds and that the code is syntactically well-formed via `cargo fmt` and careful review.
steps: Add crates.io dependencies to hybrid-orchestrator/crates/providers/Cargo.toml as CONCRETE version literals (NOT `{ workspace = true }` - providers is being moved to `[workspace] exclude` so it has no workspace root to inherit from). Add path deps on `domain` and `secrets`. Needed deps: reqwest (with features json, stream, and a rustls-tls or default TLS - pick rustls-tls to avoid OS openssl on Windows CI), futures / futures-util (for BoxStream), tokio, async-trait, serde, serde_json, thiserror. For P2.9 Bedrock SigV4 add aws-sigv4 + aws-credential-types (or aws-smithy equivalents) - choose crates that are pure Rust and Windows-friendly. Add bytes if needed for streaming. Add dev-deps for mocking HTTP+SSE: wiremock (async HTTP mock server) and/or httpmock; tokio with macros/rt for #[tokio::test]. Keep versions consistent with root [workspace.dependencies] where the dep already appears (serde=1, serde_json=1, tokio=1, thiserror=2, async-trait=0.1).

In hybrid-orchestrator/Cargo.toml: MOVE `crates/providers` OUT of `members` and INTO `exclude`. Update the surrounding explanatory comments to note that providers joined the excluded set in Phase 2 because it now carries crates.io HTTP/SSE/SigV4 deps, mirroring the wording used for the other excluded crates. Leave `mcp-client` and `routing` as the remaining offline members. Do NOT touch [workspace.dependencies] beyond optionally adding reqwest/futures/aws-sigv4 entries for future-member documentation (optional; excluded crate cannot consume them anyway).

In .github/workflows/ci.yml: add a `cargo fmt (check, providers)` step (via --manifest-path crates/providers/Cargo.toml --check) alongside the other per-crate fmt steps, and add `cargo build`, `cargo clippy (--all-targets -- -D warnings)`, and `cargo test` steps for `--manifest-path crates/providers/Cargo.toml`, placed logically near the other excluded-crate steps. Add an explanatory comment block for providers mirroring the existing per-crate comment blocks (why excluded, what deps, that tests use mocked HTTP not live network). Do NOT re-add macOS to the matrix.

Implement P2.1 in crates/providers/src/contract.rs per architecture.md Section 4.1: the `#[async_trait::async_trait] pub trait ChatProvider: Send + Sync` with methods id(&self)->&str, capabilities(&self, model:&str)->Capabilities, async list_models()->Result<Vec<ModelInfo>,ProviderError>, async chat(ChatRequest)->Result<ChatResponse,ProviderError>, async chat_stream(ChatRequest)->Result<BoxStream<'static,Result<ChatDelta,ProviderError>>,ProviderError>. Define ChatRequest{model,messages:Vec<ChatMessage>,tools:Vec<ToolSpec>,temperature:Option<f32>,max_tokens:Option<u32>,stream:bool,extra:serde_json::Value}, ChatMessage (OpenAI-shaped: role + content + optional tool_calls/tool_call_id/name), ToolSpec (function name/description/JSON-schema parameters), ChatResponse (choices/message/usage/finish_reason OpenAI-shaped), ChatDelta (incremental content + optional tool-call delta + finish reason), Capabilities{streaming,tools,vision,json_mode,max_context:Option<u32>}, ModelInfo{id, plus display/context/etc as useful}, and ProviderError (thiserror enum: transport/http-status/decode/unsupported-capability/auth/other). Use serde derives; keep the internal shape OpenAI-compatible. Add unit tests for serde round-trips of the request/response/delta shapes.

Implement P2.3 in crates/providers/src/capability.rs per Section 4.4: Capabilities descriptors (reuse the type from contract.rs or define here and re-export - keep one canonical definition) plus a capability-negotiation helper that, given a ChatRequest and a model's Capabilities, gates features: if tools unsupported, strip tools; if streaming unsupported, signal fallback to non-streaming; gate vision/json_mode; expose max_context. Also build the SHARED reusable HTTP + SSE streaming client used by all native-compatible adapters: an async fn/struct that POSTs a JSON body with headers to a base_url path and returns either a decoded JSON body (non-streaming) or a BoxStream of parsed SSE `data:` events (streaming), with `[DONE]` terminating the stream and JSON-per-event parsing. Keep it adapter-agnostic (adapters supply path, headers, body, and a per-event parse closure). Add unit tests for the negotiation logic and for SSE frame parsing (feed a fixture byte buffer of `data: {...}\n\n` frames incl. `[DONE]` and assert deltas). Do NOT hit real network in tests.

Implement P2.2 in crates/providers/src/registry.rs per Section 4.2/4.5: reuse domain::ProviderConfig and domain::ProviderKind (import from the `domain` crate; do NOT redefine them). Define `pub trait ProviderFactory: Send + Sync { fn kind(&self)->ProviderKind; fn build(&self, cfg:&ProviderConfig, secrets:&dyn secrets::SecretStore)->Result<Arc<dyn ChatProvider>,ProviderError>; }` and `pub struct ProviderRegistry { factories: HashMap<ProviderKind, Box<dyn ProviderFactory>>, instances: HashMap<String, Arc<dyn ChatProvider>> }` with methods to register a factory, build/instantiate a provider from a ProviderConfig row (resolving api_key_ref through the SecretStore at build time - never storing plaintext), get an instance by id, and list instances. Support building instances from persisted ProviderConfig rows (accept a slice/iterator of ProviderConfig). Add unit tests using a dummy ProviderFactory + a fake ChatProvider + secrets::InMemorySecretStore to prove registration, build-from-config, and secret resolution wiring (mock; no network).

Update crates/providers/src/lib.rs: replace the placeholder marker. Keep `pub mod contract; pub mod registry; pub mod capability; pub mod adapters { ... }`. Re-export the key public types (ChatProvider, ChatRequest, ChatResponse, ChatDelta, ChatMessage, ToolSpec, Capabilities, ModelInfo, ProviderError, ProviderRegistry, ProviderFactory) at the crate root for ergonomic use by tauri-app. Leave the adapter modules as placeholders for FEAT-002/003 but ensure they compile (empty or stub). Add `#[allow(dead_code)]` with a 'wired in FEAT-002/003/004' note ONLY where an item is defined-but-not-yet-constructed and would trip clippy -D warnings; remove such allows as items become used in later features.

Run `cargo fmt --manifest-path crates/providers/Cargo.toml` to format. From hybrid-orchestrator/ run `cargo build --workspace`, `cargo test --workspace`, and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` to confirm the OFFLINE members (mcp-client, routing) still build/test/clippy green after providers left the members set. The providers crate itself cannot be compiled offline (crates.io 403) - do NOT attempt to fetch; record that its compile/test/clippy is deferred to CI.
acceptance_criteria: hybrid-orchestrator/Cargo.toml lists `crates/providers` under `exclude` and NOT under `members`; `mcp-client` and `routing` remain the only members.

.github/workflows/ci.yml has fmt-check, build, clippy (-D warnings), and test steps for `--manifest-path crates/providers/Cargo.toml`, with an explanatory comment block mirroring the other excluded crates; matrix remains [ubuntu-latest, windows-latest].

contract.rs defines ChatProvider (async trait) + ChatRequest/ChatResponse/ChatDelta/ChatMessage/ToolSpec/Capabilities/ModelInfo/ProviderError matching Section 4.1 signatures, with serde derives and passing unit tests.
capability.rs provides capability negotiation (gates tools/streaming/vision/json_mode) and a shared HTTP+SSE client with SSE frame parsing covered by unit tests using fixtures (no network).

registry.rs implements ProviderRegistry + ProviderFactory reusing domain::ProviderConfig/ProviderKind, builds instances from ProviderConfig rows resolving api_key_ref via SecretStore, with unit tests using InMemorySecretStore.
From hybrid-orchestrator/: `cargo build --workspace`, `cargo test --workspace`, and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` all pass (offline members).
verification: From hybrid-orchestrator/: `cargo build --workspace` (offline members still green after providers moved to exclude)
`cargo fmt --manifest-path crates/providers/Cargo.toml --check` (formatting of the new networked crate; note: does not compile deps offline, only formats)
Manual review confirms Cargo.toml members/exclude change and ci.yml per-manifest providers steps mirror the documented existing pattern; providers compile/test/clippy deferred to CI.
findings:
IMPLEMENTED (P2.1/P2.2/P2.3 + workspace/CI restructure):
- hybrid-orchestrator/Cargo.toml: moved crates/providers from `members` to `exclude` (alongside domain/orchestrator-core/persistence/secrets/tauri-app); mcp-client + routing remain the only offline members. Updated the members/exclude explanatory comments to record that providers joined the excluded set in Phase 2 because it now carries crates.io HTTP/SSE/SigV4 deps. Added documentation-only reqwest/futures/futures-util/bytes/aws-sigv4/aws-credential-types entries to [workspace.dependencies] (excluded crate cannot consume them; pins its own concrete literals).
- crates/providers/Cargo.toml: concrete-literal deps (NOT `{workspace=true}`; excluded crate has no workspace root): domain+secrets path deps; reqwest 0.12 with default-features=false + [json, stream, rustls-tls] (rustls chosen to avoid OS OpenSSL on Windows CI); futures/futures-util 0.3, bytes 1, tokio 1 (rt,macros), async-trait 0.1, serde/serde_json/thiserror; aws-sigv4 1 + aws-credential-types 1 for later Bedrock (P2.9). dev-deps: wiremock 0.6 + tokio (rt,rt-multi-thread,macros).
- .github/workflows/ci.yml: added `cargo fmt (check, providers)` next to the other per-crate fmt-checks, and a per-manifest providers block (build, clippy --all-targets -D warnings, test) near the other excluded crates, with an explanatory comment block mirroring the existing ones (why excluded, which deps, tests use mocked HTTP+SSE). Also added providers to the top-of-file excluded-crate list comment. Matrix left as [ubuntu-latest, windows-latest] (macOS not re-added).
- contract.rs (P2.1): `#[async_trait] ChatProvider` with id/capabilities/list_models/chat/chat_stream matching Section 4.1; ChatRequest, ChatMessage (role+content+tool_calls+tool_call_id+name), ToolSpec/FunctionSpec, ChatResponse/ChatChoice, ChatDelta/ToolCallDelta, ToolCall/FunctionCall, Capabilities (canonical here), ModelInfo, Usage, FinishReason, MessageRole, and a thiserror ProviderError (Transport/HttpStatus/Decode/UnsupportedCapability/Auth/Other). serde derives throughout + serde round-trip unit tests. NOTE: ToolSpec/FunctionSpec deliberately derive PartialEq but NOT Eq because they carry serde_json::Value (Value is not Eq); same for ChatRequest.
- capability.rs (P2.3): `negotiate()` gating (strip tools, streaming fallback flag, strip json_mode response_format, surface max_context) returning a `Negotiated`; re-exports Capabilities from contract. Shared adapter-agnostic `HttpSseClient` (post_json non-streaming, post_sse streaming) plus a reusable `sse_event_stream` SSE decoder built on futures_util::stream::unfold (handles LF and CRLF frame boundaries, multi-line data:, comment/keepalive lines, `[DONE]` termination). Unit tests cover negotiation branches and SSE parsing from fixture byte buffers split across chunk boundaries (no network).
- registry.rs (P2.2): `ProviderFactory` trait (kind/build with &dyn secrets::SecretStore) and `ProviderRegistry` (factories + instances) reusing domain::ProviderConfig/ProviderKind (not redefined). Methods: register_factory, has_factory, build_from_config, build_all (from ProviderConfig rows), get, instance_ids, instances. Secrets resolved through SecretStore at build time (never stored plaintext). Unit tests use a dummy factory + fake ChatProvider + secrets::InMemorySecretStore proving registration, build-from-config, build-all, secret resolution wiring, and missing-factory error (no network).
- lib.rs: replaced placeholder; re-exports the key public types + domain::ProviderConfig/ProviderKind; adapter modules kept as compiling stubs for FEAT-002/003/004.
No `#[allow(dead_code)]` was needed (all defined items are exercised by tests/re-exports).

VERIFIED OFFLINE (from hybrid-orchestrator/): `cargo build --workspace`, `cargo test --workspace`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` all PASS (these now cover only mcp-client + routing after providers left members). `cargo fmt --manifest-path crates/providers/Cargo.toml --check` reports NO diffs. Cargo.lock updated (providers entry removed as it left the workspace) - committed as part of the change. Confirmed `cargo build --manifest-path crates/providers/Cargo.toml --offline` fails only at crates.io dependency resolution (manifest parses fine), matching the INTEGRATIONS_ONLY 403 constraint.

DEFERRED TO CI (network-only, by design): the providers crate's actual compile/test/clippy runs via the new `--manifest-path crates/providers/Cargo.toml` CI steps on ubuntu + windows. Code was written carefully for first-compile-in-CI correctness (e.g. dropped Eq where serde_json::Value is present; rustls-tls to avoid Windows OpenSSL).
